chunks: And in the narration of Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
It is obligatory upon the Imam to imprison the corrupt among the scholars, the ignorant among the physicians, and the incompetent among the nobles.
And he (peace be upon him) said: The Imam's imprisonment after the fixed punishment (has been carried out) is injustice.

key_terms.الْفُسَّاقَ: The corrupt or wicked (plural of fasiq)
key_terms.الْمَفَالِيسَ: The incompetent or lacking skill (plural of mafalisa)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between administrative imprisonment and fixed punishment in Shia jurisprudence according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Barqi distinguishes between administrative detention (habb) for professional incompetence or social misconduct and judicial punishment (hadd), emphasizing that the Imam must detain corrupt scholars, ignorant physicians, and incompetent nobles to maintain public order. It further clarifies that once the fixed legal punishment has been executed, further detention constitutes injustice. This highlights the Imam's role in ensuring competence and accountability across various social strata, a key aspect of Shia governance theory.
